claims.text: The signature move: training loss equals evaluation loss, LightGBM's custom objective hands the booster the analytic [[QLIKE]] gradient 1 - exp(y_true - y_pred) and hessian exp(y_true - y_pred) in log-RV space, so trees split on the exact metric the tournament scores.

    Previously this divided by sqrt(h) to convert the 24h-tenor Kvar into a

    and the RV forecast (annualized via sqrt(252 * daily_var)) are already in

claims.text: Modules are laid out as the forecasting pipeline reads: volforecast.data ingests, features transforms, models fits, evaluation scores and cli drives, with the shared volforecast.utils at the highest fan-in in the repo, so imports flow the same direction the data does.

Errors are contained where they happen: Optuna workers catch exceptions so one failed trial cannot kill a tuning study, ingestion writes parquet atomically via a staging directory and merges rather than overwrites, and the audit command signals problems with a non-zero exit code.

The heterogeneous autoregressive baseline: regress tomorrow's log RV on the daily value `log_rv_d`, the 5 day mean `log_rv_w`, and the 22 day mean `log_rv_m`. Three coefficients, brutally hard to beat, and the benchmark every ML model in the tournament is scored against.

A microstructure-noise-robust variance estimator that weights return autocovariances with a flat-top Parzen kernel. On clean prices it agrees with 5 minute RV; on noisy tick data it recovers true variance where naive tick-by-tick RV is inflated.

The `__init__` docstring declares it plainly: progressively enrich [[HAR]]-family baselines with microstructure, options-implied, and cross-asset features via gradient boosting until the [[QLIKE]] improvement is statistically significant and the IV-RV gap is tradeable. `__main__.py` routes every `vol run --config` invocation through the tournament code path, one model or thirteen, and every run ends in an interactive Plotly dashboard.

role: Eighteen registered feature layers turn daily realized measures and enriched market columns into the design matrix every tabular model trains on. The numbered spine runs from Layer 0, the [[HAR]] backbone of log [[realized variance]] lags, through asymmetry, options, microstructure, and cross-asset layers, to the Layer 5 calendar. Each layer is a class registered under a short name via `register_feature_layer`, so a config stacks layers declaratively through `FEATURE_REGISTRY` instead of importing them.

The layers here span three information sources. `options.py` extracts forward looking signals from the SPX [[implied volatility]] surface: the variance risk premium as squared ATM implied vol minus annualized realized variance, the 25-delta risk reversal, term slope, and butterfly convexity. `microstructure.py` distills order flow from cached 10 second bars: Kyle's lambda, the OLS slope of price changes on signed volume, plus the Amihud illiquidity ratio, volume concentration, and flow persistence. `calendar.py` encodes scheduled events: FOMC, NFP, and OpEx proximity in trading days.

The distinctive discipline is leakage control at the feature level: features built from market data are lagged one day before use, while calendar features are deliberately not shifted because event dates are known in advance, and `day_of_week` and `month` stay integer dtype so LightGBM treats them as categoricals. NFP is derived as the first Friday of each month and OpEx as the third, while FOMC dates are hardcoded through 2026 with a distance fallback of 30 beyond them.

    VRP = (atm_iv_pct / 100)^2 - rv_daily * 252

role: Point-in-time graph construction for the graph-based volatility models. The rule that defines the package: a graph used to forecast date t is estimated on data up to t only, re-estimated every 21 trading days on a trailing 252-day window, and frozen between refits, so the network structure itself cannot leak the future. `build_graph_schedule` turns any builder into such a schedule, and dates with too little history get an empty snapshot rather than a peek ahead.

Every builder satisfies the `GraphBuilder` protocol and returns an immutable `GraphSnapshot`: COO edge indices and float32 weights over an ordered symbol tuple. Numpy-first by design: linear models like GHAR consume dense adjacencies without importing torch, and neural models call `to_torch()`. Estimated builders (correlation threshold, kNN, GLASSO, the directed Diebold-Yilmaz spillover graph) sit alongside the structural controls in simple.py, where identity is the no-graph control: GHAR on the identity graph equals plain pooled [[HAR]].

diagnostics.py watches two published failure modes, crisis density explosion of thresholded correlation graphs and GLASSO edge instability across refits, tracked as consecutive-refit edge-set Jaccard. It also supplies the magnetic Laplacian and graph signal energy diagnostics that back the GSP-HAR model.

role: The model zoo of `volforecast`: every forecaster the tournament can run, registered under a string name in `MODEL_REGISTRY` so a YAML config picks models by name alone. The families span nine naive baselines that set the [[QLIKE]] floor, the linear [[HAR]] family (its registration file is missing from this snapshot), gradient boosting via LightGBM, its DART dropout variant, and XGBoost, a seven-model graph suite, and five ensembles from seed bagging to a regime-dependent blend.

The signature move is that training loss equals evaluation loss. LightGBM and XGBoost train on a hand-derived QLIKE custom objective, gradient 1 - exp(y_true - y_pred) and hessian exp(y_true - y_pred) in log RV space, and the torch graph models share a `_qlike_loss` of the same form, so trees split and gradients descend on the exact metric the tournament ranks by, one that penalizes under-predicting volatility harder than over-predicting it.

Tuning is industrial: Optuna searches run under walk-forward expanding-window CV to prevent look-ahead bias, with parallel worker processes coordinated through journal storage and, for XGBoost, each worker pinned round-robin to its own GPU. The `gnn` model treats every trading date as one graph snapshot, symbols as nodes and rolling-correlation edges, learning cross-asset volatility spillovers with GATv2 attention and flagging `requires_graph = True` so the pipeline runner dispatches graph data instead of tabular features.

src-volforecast-models.feeds: Out-of-sample log RV predictions per fold into `evaluation`, where the tournament ranks every model by QLIKE and backs the ranking with statistical tests.

role: Fold-level orchestration that sits between the CV splitters and the models, built to make leakage structurally difficult. Every step runs inside the fold that owns it: `feature_selection.py` does Boruta-style TreeSHAP shadow selection, keeping only features whose mean absolute SHAP beats a threshold set by permuted shadow copies of themselves, and `norm.py` fits per-symbol z-score normalisers from training rows alone so one symbol's vol regime cannot contaminate another's scaling.

`fold_cache.py` content-addresses expensive LSTM and TCN training: a deterministic fingerprint over config, horizon, fold number, train and test date hashes, and base-model predictions decides whether a fold can be skipped, so nothing retrains by accident and a change to any input invalidates exactly the right cache entries. `conditional_duan.py` then upgrades the global Duan log-to-level bias correction to a per-sample one, training a lightweight XGBoost variance model on OOS residuals from strictly prior folds, or reading squared VVIX as a direct uncertainty proxy.

src-volforecast-pipeline.feeds: Leakage-controlled inputs into `models` and bias-corrected predictions into `evaluation`, where the tournament ranks everything by QLIKE.

"""Apply conditional Duan correction using walk-forward variance estimation.

    For each fold k, trains a variance model on squared OOS residuals from
    folds 1..k-1, then predicts σ²(x) for fold k's test samples and applies:

        pred_corrected = pred_original + σ²_hat(x) / 2

    This redistributes the correction across samples based on estimated
    conditional variance: high-uncertainty days get more, calm days get less.

role: The foundation drawer, imported by ten module groups and importing none of them back. Its centerpiece is `cv.py`, the leakage firewall: purged k-fold deletes observations within a purge gap of each test block so overlapping realized volatility windows cannot leak, blocked k-fold keeps contiguous time blocks, expanding and rolling windows walk forward, and `PanelExpandingWindowCV` splits the panel on unique dates so every symbol on a date lands in the same fold. Random k-fold is banned as look-ahead bias.

`manifest.py` is the data ledger with two layers, a contract stating what data should exist (expected columns, value bounds, a NaN budget) and a state recording what does exist per symbol. Ingest commands update the state and `vol audit` validates it against the contract, through a typed YAML `ManifestManager` plus legacy JSON wrappers kept alive during migration.

`persistence.py` is the experiment memory: it writes fitted models, out-of-sample predictions, and a consolidated metrics.json under data/models/, then fingerprints every training-relevant config field plus each symbol's data file so a rerun with nothing changed skips retraining, and `check_fingerprint` names exactly what changed when the hashes disagree.

src-volforecast-utils.feeds: Ten module groups build on it: ingestion records into the manifest, model training runs inside its CV splits, and evaluation, reporting, and the CLI read the predictions, metrics, and fingerprints it persists.

class PurgedKFoldCV(_BaseCVSplitter):
    """Purged k-fold cross-validation for time series.

    Splits data into k contiguous folds and purges observations
    within a gap window between training and test sets to prevent
    information leakage from overlapping RV windows.

    ``embargo`` (Phase 2.8): rows in ``[test_end, test_end + embargo)`` are also
    excluded from the train sets of all SUBSEQUENT folds. Default 0 (no-op).
    """

tour.text: Start here. Every interaction is a `vol` subcommand: one primary command, `vol run --config`, drives ingest, training, and evaluation from a single YAML file, and around it sit the ingest, audit, and live forecast commands. Each subcommand registers itself, so the surface grows without touching the entry point.

The zoo: naive baselines that set the floor, LightGBM and XGBoost trained on a custom [[QLIKE]] objective, and a graph suite whose controls deliberately nest the simpler models. One shared contract means a random walk and a graph attention network take the same walk through the same folds.

The design matrix factory: layered feature classes turn daily measures into model inputs, from [[HAR]] lags through options-implied signals like the [[variance risk premium]] to calendar effects. A config stacks layers by name; the registry finds them.

The HTML experiment report, honestly unfinished: most sections are documented stubs, and the one real section prices the forecasts with the realistic straddle engine, lagging implied vol by a day to avoid look-ahead.
The smallest box on the board: what survives here renders model lineage as a flowchart for dashboards. The dashboard builder itself is one of the modules this snapshot lost.

The anti-cheating layer: per-symbol normalisers fitted on training rows only, a fingerprint-keyed cache that decides when an expensive fold may be skipped, and a per-sample Duan correction estimated strictly walk-forward from earlier folds.

The heaviest lifting: ticks from Chunk Store, daily series from TSDB, the SPX vol surface from Marquee, all cached as per-symbol parquet. Its estimators turn millions of ticks into the daily [[realized variance]] panel everything downstream trains on.

The hub. The registry maps model, feature, and graph names to classes, which is why most of the repo imports this tiny package: a YAML config names components, the registry turns names into code, and the tournament routing lives beside it.

Where claims go to die: [[QLIKE]] ranking, Diebold-Mariano tests, the Model Confidence Set, then the money tests, realistic delta-hedged straddles and the GSVIVS01 signal, with Sharpe ratios deflated for selection luck.

Point-in-time graph construction for the graph models: a graph used to forecast a date is estimated only on data up to that date, re-estimated on a schedule, and frozen between refits, so the network structure itself cannot leak the future.

Last, the quiet foundation: paths.py anchors every cache to the repo root, and cv.py holds the purged and walk-forward splitters that keep every result honest. Everything above imports these seven files; nothing here imports back.
